historical_record.description: The Art Commission approved the working drawings for the Larsen Square Swimming Pool, designed by William Gladstone Merchant.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build the Larsen Park swimming pool to Engstrum & Nourse at $350,880, the lowest of several bids.

The Recreation and Park Commission named the swimming pool in Larsen Park for Charlie Sava, the swimming instructor, with plaques in the pool to tell both his story and that of Carl G. Larsen, who gave the city the park.

After testing found dangerously high lead levels in the jet plane that served as a play structure at Larsen Park, with repair put at $40,000 to $50,000 and soil cleanup at up to $100,000 more, the Recreation and Park Commission approved removing the plane; a museum had offered to take it at no cost.

The Board of Park Commissioners received the Supervisors' resolution asking the Mayor to set a day to dedicate the land the late Carl G. Larsen had deeded to the city for a park, in the blocks between Ulloa and Wawona Streets and Nineteenth and Twentieth Avenues.
